title.es: Voz narrativa y punto de vista

es: Reconocer la voz narrativa (primera persona, tercera limitada u omnisciente) en fragmentos breves y justificarla con una pista.

teaching.en: I open the letter and my hands tremble, but I cannot say what my sister feels, because a first-person narrator only knows his or her own mind and sees events from a single vantage point.
teaching.es: Abro la carta y me tiemblan las manos, pero no puedo decir qué siente mi hermana, porque un narrador en primera persona solo conoce su propia mente y ve los hechos desde un único punto de vista.
teaching.explanationEs: El pronombre I es la pista de la primera persona: el narrador es un personaje y solo cuenta lo que vive y siente.
segments: I open the letter and my hands tremble, but I cannot say what my sister feels, because a
first-person narrator only knows his or her own mind and sees events from a single vantage point.
teaching.audioText: I open the letter and my hands tremble, but I cannot say what my sister feels, because a first-person narrator only knows his or her own mind and sees events from a single vantage point.

teaching.en: Mara opens the letter and wonders why her father has written after so many years, yet the narrator never steps inside his mind.
teaching.es: Mara abre la carta y se pregunta por qué ha escrito su padre después de tantos años, pero el narrador nunca entra en la mente de él.
teaching.explanationEs: Tercera persona limitada: el narrador sigue a Mara y solo conocemos sus pensamientos.
segments: Mara opens the letter and wonders why her father has written after
so many years, yet the narrator never steps inside his mind.
teaching.audioText: Mara opens the letter and wonders why her father has written after so many years, yet the narrator never steps inside his mind.

teaching.en: An omniscient narrator is privy to every character's thoughts, so the reader learns what Mara fears and what her father is hiding.
teaching.es: Un narrador omnisciente está al tanto de los pensamientos de todos los personajes, así que el lector sabe lo que teme Mara y lo que oculta su padre.
teaching.explanationEs: Omniscient: el narrador entra en varias mentes a la vez; be privy to significa estar al tanto de algo reservado.
segments: An omniscient narrator is privy to every character's thoughts, so the
reader learns what Mara fears and what her father is hiding.
teaching.audioText: An omniscient narrator is privy to every character's thoughts, so the reader learns what Mara fears and what her father is hiding.

teaching.en: A limited narrator shows one mind only, whereas an omniscient one moves freely between several minds and sometimes comments on events from a distance.
teaching.es: Un narrador limitado muestra una sola mente, mientras que uno omnisciente se mueve con libertad entre varias y a veces comenta los hechos desde lejos.
teaching.explanationEs: Limited y omniscient se distinguen por cuántas mentes abre el narrador; whereas contrasta los dos tipos.
segments: A limited narrator shows one mind only, whereas an omniscient one moves
freely between several minds and sometimes comments on events from a distance.
teaching.audioText: A limited narrator shows one mind only, whereas an omniscient one moves freely between several minds and sometimes comments on events from a distance.

teaching.en: An unreliable narrator may mislead you, so look for any clue that can reveal the gap between what he claims and what really happened.
teaching.es: Un narrador poco fiable puede engañarte, así que busca cualquier pista que revele la diferencia entre lo que afirma y lo que realmente ocurrió.
teaching.explanationEs: Unreliable describe a quien cuenta con sesgo o mentiras; mislead es inducir a error a quien lee.
segments: An unreliable narrator may mislead you, so look for any clue that
can reveal the gap between what he claims and what really happened.
teaching.audioText: An unreliable narrator may mislead you, so look for any clue that can reveal the gap between what he claims and what really happened.

teaching.en: The tone may be warm or detached, and that voice, more than the pronoun alone, tells you how much the narrator cares about the characters.
teaching.es: El tono puede ser cálido o distante, y esa voz, más que el pronombre por sí solo, te dice cuánto le importan los personajes al narrador.
teaching.explanationEs: La voz narrativa es el tono y la actitud de quien cuenta; detached significa sin implicación emocional.
segments: The tone may be warm or detached, and that voice, more than the
pronoun alone, tells you how much the narrator cares about the characters.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué muestra que solo conocemos la mente de quien cuenta?

choices.text: The pronoun I is used, and the narrator cannot tell what the sister thinks.
The pronoun I is used, and the narrator reports what the sister secretly feels.
The pronoun I is avoided, and the narrator describes how the sister feels.

feedback.es: El narrador dice I y admite que no sabe si su hermana ya la leyó: solo accede a su propia mente.

hint.es: Busca el pronombre y comprueba si el narrador sabe lo que piensa su hermana.

origin.text: I opened the letter slowly, afraid of what it might say. In the next room my sister was singing, and I could not tell whether she had already read it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Este es un narrador limitado, no omnisciente.»

feedback.es: Un narrador que sigue una sola mente y no entra en la de los demás es limitado.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo contrario a omniscient: solo se abre una mente.

origin.text: We only ever see the story through Mara's eyes, and we never learn what her brother feels. This is a ___ narrator, not an omniscient one.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El narrador está al tanto de los pensamientos de cada personaje.»

answer.text: The narrator is privy to every character's thoughts

feedback.es: Be privy to va seguido de lo que el narrador conoce; every character's thoughts cierra la frase.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y sigue con is privy to.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué sabemos del hermano de quien narra.

choices.text: What he privately thinks about the letter, as the narrator explains.
Only his teasing, since the narrator cannot know what he thinks.
That he also received a letter from the grandfather years before.

feedback.es: El narrador solo cuenta cómo lo molestaba su hermano; no puede saber qué piensa, porque cuenta desde su propia mente.

origin.audio: When I was twelve, my grandfather handed me a letter and made me promise not to open it until I was older. I carried it for years, and whenever I touched the envelope my hands would tremble. My brother teased me about it constantly, but I never told him what I suspected: that the letter was not a goodbye at all, but an apology. I still wonder whether I was right.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender quien narra sobre la carta.

choices.text: That it was a goodbye, exactly as the grandfather had explained.
That it should have been opened sooner, as the brother insisted.
That it may hold an apology, although nobody has confirmed it.

feedback.es: Quien narra sospecha que era una disculpa, pero termina con «I still wonder»: es una sospecha sin confirmar.

origin.audio: When I was twelve, my grandfather handed me a letter and made me promise not to open it until I was older. prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con su tipo de narrador.

pairs: I never told anyone how afraid I was that evening.
We argued all night, and none of us dared to say what we feared.
She checked the map again, wondering if Leo had lied.
Mara feared the answer, while her father rehearsed his excuse.

feedback.es: El pronombre (I, we, she) y el número de mentes que se abren distinguen cada tipo de narrador.

pairs: I never told anyone how afraid I was that evening.
We argued all night, and none of us dared to say what we feared.
She checked the map again, wondering if Leo had lied.
Mara feared the answer, while her father rehearsed his excuse.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué muestra que el narrador es omnisciente.

choices.text: The narrator reports the father's secret plans while Mara knows nothing about them.
The narrator uses the pronoun she, which always marks an omniscient voice.
The narrator describes the rain and the window from far away, like a camera.

feedback.es: El narrador cuenta lo que el padre planea en secreto mientras Mara lo ignora: entra en dos mentes a la vez.

origin.audio: The rain had not stopped all week. Mara sat by the window, convinced that her father had forgotten her birthday. Across town, he was wrapping the gift he had hidden for months, rehearsing what he would say. Neither of them suspected that the other was thinking about the same old photo, taken years before the argument.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué efecto consigue el narrador al abrir dos mentes.

choices.text: The reader learns that the father is lying to his daughter about the gift.
The reader sees a misunderstanding that neither character can see.
The reader expects Mara to forgive her father without any help.

feedback.es: Solo el lector sabe que ambos piensan en la misma foto y que el padre no la ha olvidado: ve lo que ellos no ven.

prompt.es: Completa: «…los críticos llaman al narrador poco fiable.»

feedback.es: Cuando el relato de quien cuenta choca con los hechos, se le llama narrador poco fiable (unreliable).

origin.text: He insists that he was at home all evening, yet everyone remembers seeing him at the harbour, so critics call the narrator ___.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué actitud transmite la voz del narrador hacia el comité?

choices.text: Warm respect: he praises the patience of every member.
Anxious concern: he fears that the decision will be delayed again.
Ironic distance: he watches the meeting with quiet humour.

feedback.es: «As committees do» y «to decide nothing» muestran una distancia irónica: observa con humor, sin implicarse.

origin.text: The committee met, as committees do, to decide nothing. Mr Hale spoke for an hour; the others nodded, looked at their watches and thought about lunch. By noon the agenda had been approved, and the real problem had, naturally, been left for next week.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué indica que el narrador solo sigue a Tom?

choices.text: We learn Tom's fears, but Ana's reaction stays unknown.
We learn Ana's anger, which she hides from Tom behind the door.
We hear Tom himself say I, so the story comes from his own voice.

feedback.es: El lector conoce los miedos de Tom, pero no puede saber lo que siente Ana tras la puerta: hay una sola mente abierta.

origin.text: Tom waited outside the door, rehearsing his apology. Surely Ana would never forgive him; he had ruined everything. He called her name twice, but he could not tell whether the silence meant anger or sleep.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un narrador poco fiable puede engañar al lector al omitir cosas.»

feedback.es: Mislead significa engañar o inducir a error: lo que el narrador calla puede desviar al lector.

origin.text: Notice what the narrator refuses to mention. An unreliable narrator may ___ the reader by leaving out exactly what he wants to hide.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué sugiere sobre el narrador.

choices.text: That he is an omniscient observer with access to every mind.
That he knows more than he admits, so he may not be honest.
That he is honest but tends to exaggerate small details.

feedback.es: Conoce demasiados detalles para alguien que apenas conocía a la víctima: el lector duda de él, como ante un narrador poco fiable.

origin.audio: Our narrator insists that he hardly knew the man, yet he describes the man's habits, his money problems and even his favourite chair in great detail. He claims to be only curious, but the reader begins to wonder.
